title: Medical Science Does Not Change Crossing Borders, But Do Standards of Human Decency? Comparing the U.S. And Canada

content_html_sanitized:
In yesterday’s posting, Progress-Of-A-Sort - On Medical Cannabis Policy In Europe, But For Real in the Czech Republic,  I made what should be an obvious point, “Medical science does not change when it crosses borders. Cannabis works exactly the same in Spain, or France or Germany….Or even in The Netherlands!!!” Or, I should have added, Canada.

 

Although the Canadian medical system is largely a government service, the practice of medicine is very similar in all western countries, obviously including the United States.

 

Medical science really is a science. So, Canada’s experience with medical cannabis is entirely applicable to the practice of medicine in the United States (and the rest of the world). Ignoring Canadian experience is particularly egregious given our proximity and cultural similarities. From the Government of Canada: Medical Use of Cannabis

 

I have written frequently about our shameful treatment of our disabled veterans, but I still cannot believe that we are still abusing so shamefully the people who have suffered so much to defend our freedoms.

See

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

And

Veterans Who Fought for Our Freedom May Finally Get Medical Cannabis

 

However, today I stumbled upon a webpage from the Canadian Government, regarding how our neighbors really do take care of their veterans, putting to shame the American people. This is how it should be done. This is how it must be done.

 

Cannabis for Medical Purposes: “The health and well-being of Veterans are top priorities for the Government of Canada. This is why Veterans Affairs Canada developed a cannabis for medical purposes reimbursement policy, taking into account input that the Department received from Veterans, their advocates, stakeholders, medical experts, as well as existing research on using cannabis for medical purposes.”

From the DAV: Marijuana in Veterans’ Medical Treatment Medical cannabis as an alternative to opioids for veterans

And from NORML: Marijuana and Veterans Issues
